result.summary: Executed docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-019.md against branch feature/WF02-REQ-019 at commit e804213. npm run lint: 0 errors (2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings, unrelated to this diff). npm run build: both workspaces clean (Next.js build compiled successfully; tsc -p tsconfig.json for apps/bot clean). npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (per ISS-0014): 26 files / 288 tests passed. Named unit re-runs per AC all passed individually (profile.test.ts -t "AC1's own case"/"AC2"/"AC6", onboarding.test.ts -t "consent-needed wins"/"ready (AC4)"). AC1 (kill+restart resumes at the next field): built two genuinely separate npx tsx processes (scratch-verify-req019-ac1-phase1.ts, scratch-verify-req019-ac1-phase2.ts, no import/reference between them). Phase 1 launched backgrounded via bash job control, printed 'PROCESS_READY_TO_KILL pid=38488' (found after 2 x 1s bounded poll iterations, cap 30). Confirmed the PID was a real live node.exe via tasklist before killing. Force-terminated with `taskkill /F /PID 38488` (Windows equivalent of a forceful SIGKILL, not a graceful shutdown) -- output 'SUCCESS: ... terminated'. Confirmed the process was genuinely gone (not merely that the kill command returned) via a bounded tasklist poll immediately after -- 'No tasks are running which match the specified criteria' on the very first check. Read-back immediately after the kill showed the 3 pre-kill answers (first_name/last_name/company) committed and survived the hard kill, with position/is_student/experience_level still NULL. Phase 2, a wholly independent process with its own freshly-empty `captured` array, dispatched a 4th answer ('Some Position') and its only sendMessage was the isStudent prompt -- proving it accepted the dispatch as the position answer purely by reading Postgres (no in-process memory of what was already asked) and correctly advanced past it, without re-prompting any of the first three fields. Read-back after phase 2 confirmed all three pre-kill values byte-for-byte unchanged plus the new position value. AC1b/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC-schema/AC-catalog: all executed as live single-process dispatch cases (or direct file reads for AC-schema/AC-catalog) per the spec's exact fixtures and dispatch sequences, with real psql read-backs after each. AC5 specifically redirected the harness's own real stdout/stderr to files (ac5-stdout.log/ac5-stderr.log) and grepped THOSE files (not the mocked Telegram captures) for the pre-existing phone value and the rejected email string -- zero matches in either. Full per-case detail, real command output summaries, and exact read-back values are in test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-019.yaml. All scratch harness files (apps/bot/scratch-verify-req019*.ts, apps/bot/ac5-stdout.log, apps/bot/ac5-stderr.log, apps/bot/ac1-phase1.log) were deleted at the end of the run; `docker compose down -v` torn down the scratch Postgres; `git status --porcelain` confirmed a clean tree before this handoff was written. One MINOR issue found and reported below (not blocking, not a product defect): AC3b's own write-up has an internal wording inconsistency between a per-bullet 'Expected: ... produces no sendMessage' line and its own AC-level Pass Conditions paragraph, which explicitly permits 'resolved to the consent prompt' as an alternative outcome for the same scenario. The actual implementation (handlers/profile.ts's makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler, which unconditionally re-derives and prompts via advanceAfterWrite on every dispatch, matched or not) correctly resolves to the consent prompt here -- verified this is intentional, identical-pattern behavior to what AC1b's own cases already exercise, and that profiles never received any read or write in either AC3b scenario, which is the AC's real gating property.

issues.title: REQ-019.md AC3b per-bullet 'Expected' wording conflicts with its own AC-level Pass Conditions paragraph
issues.description: The forged-skip-while-unconsented scenario's per-bullet 'Expected' line says the callback 'produces no sendMessage', but the AC's own overarching Pass Conditions paragraph explicitly allows 'resolved to the consent prompt' as an alternative to a silent no-op. The real implementation correctly takes the consent-prompt branch (advanceAfterWrite always re-derives and prompts), which the Pass Conditions paragraph anticipates but the narrower bullet does not. Not a product defect -- recommend the per-bullet wording be tightened to match the AC-level pass condition so a future TEST-RUNNER doesn't have to reconcile the two.
